title: A Rhythmic Definition of Prime Numbers:Multiplication defined as Counting and Phase Non-Closure
description: This paper introduces a rhythmic definition of prime numbers in which multiplication is reinterpreted as counting — a process of motion through discrete phase cycles. Numbers are modeled as trajectories within two fundamental rhythms: the 4-ladder (binary) and the 6-ladder (ternary). A number is prime if it cannot be reached exactly by any combination of these base rhythms — that is, if it represents a point of phase non-closure between the two. This definition replaces arithmetic divisibility with harmonic reachability. Primality becomes a structural property of phase alignment rather than a magnitude-dependent computation. The resulting model reveals a constant 3:2 frequency ratio — a “prime π” — governing the distribution of non-closures in additive space, analogous to π’s role in geometric non-closure. Computation within this lattice requires only additive traversal — complexity O(logN) — independent of the number’s size.
